notes.claim: A power's index says how many times the base is multiplied by itself, and the index laws apply when the bases are the same.
Fractional exponents are defined as roots, which makes sense from the rule for powers of powers.
A prefix on a unit symbol forms one new symbol that can be raised to a power, and milli is the prefix for one thousandth, 10⁻³.
A power's index shows how many times a number has been multiplied by itself.
With the same base, multiplying powers adds the indices: 9³ × 9⁵ = 9⁸.
Dividing powers of one base cancels common factors: three eights from the top and all those below leave 8 × 8, which is 8².
Raising a power to a power multiplies the indices.
Dividing by the base each time the exponent drops extends the pattern to zero and negative powers, and shows why a⁰ = 1.
Any base to the power of zero equals 1.
A negative power gives the reciprocal of the number, which is 1 over the number.
A common misconception is that a negative power makes the result negative, and it does not.
An older SQA Higher National unit, Introductory Mathematics for Engineering, asks for answers left with positive indices (added for i2's practice).
The square root symbol writes the exact side length of a square whose area is a given number of square units, such as 73.
A surd is an expression that includes a square root, cube root or other root symbol.
A rounded decimal answer such as 1.73 is not exact, so an exact answer is left as a surd.
Fractional exponents are defined as roots, which makes sense from the rule for powers of powers.
In a fractional exponent the numerator tells the power and the denominator tells the root.
Standard form is a number between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of ten, also called scientific notation.
NIST recommends choosing prefixes so values lie between 0.1 and 1000, using only prefixes for powers of 10 that are multiples of 3.
Milli is the metric prefix for one thousandth, 10⁻³.
A prefix attached to a unit symbol forms a new inseparable symbol that can be raised to a positive or negative power.
Converting between metric units of area and volume means multiplying or dividing by the factor squared for area and cubed for volume.
Heat per second in a wire carrying a current is proportional to its resistance and to the square of the current.
In an inverse square relationship, doubling the distance cuts the intensity to one quarter.
